messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: mutable data for VI, etc.
parts:
I've been thinking about how we can support streaming VB (VI, whatevs)
and it seems like the easiest thing to do would be to make the
data member variables mutable in the generated class for a Stan program.
Would that be enough? You could then set them from the outside if you
knew what they were.

That would be trivial to implement (as in I could do it by the end
of the week on a branch).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mutable data for VI, etc.
parts:
From the discussion in the last meeting, what I'd do is something like
this to select minibatches:

data {
int<lower=0> M;
int<lower=M> N;
vector[N] x;
vector[N] y;
int[M] Is; // indexes of current minibatch
}
transformed data {
real M_over_N;
M_over_N <- (1.0 * M) / N;
}
parameters {
real alpha;
real beta;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
alpha ~ normal(0, 2);
beta ~ normal(0, 2);
sigma ~ cauchy(0, 1);

increment_log_prob(M_over_N * normal(y[Is], alpha + beta * x[Is], sigma));
}

Having the data be mutable means you could reset the value of Is on
the fly. This is assuming also that y[Is] picks out the values of y
at the indices Is. That's not written yet, but I hope to have it done
soon. Until then, we could write sub_index(y,Is) instead of y[Is]
using a function like this:

vector[] sub_index(vector[] y, int[] Is) {
vector[size(Is)] y_Is;
for (i in 1:size(Is))
y_Is[i] <- y[Is[i]];
return y_Is;
}

To do full data replacement is even easier. Then all you need is
this:

data {
int<lower=0> M;
int<lower=M> N;
vector[M] x;
vector[M] y;
}
transformed data {
real M_over_N;
M_over_N <- (1.0 * M) / N;
}
parameters {
real alpha;
real beta;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
alpha ~ normal(0, 2);
beta ~ normal(0, 2);
sigma ~ cauchy(0, 1);

increment_log_prob(M_over_N * normal(y, alpha + beta * x, sigma));
}

Then you just replace all of x and y with the minibatch. The minibatches
wouldn't even need to be the same size. You could replace M, too.
But you don't even need any mods to do this. You can just write the model
as above and reconstitute it each time --- it'll be just as fast. The
constructor of the .hpp file generated just reads the data out of a var_context.

- Bob
